title: Oramics
description: Four loops of clear 35mm film run in step past one line of light, the way Daphne Oram's machine read its stack of synchronised strips. Each strip holds one control: on the top one a drawn shape's height is the pitch and its weight how loud; the second is a mask on the volume, so a swelling ribbon swells and a gap gates; the third is the waveform itself, its density down the strip read as one cycle and turned into harmonics; the fourth sets the vibrato and how far into the room it goes. Slow strokes lay down heavy ink and quick ones dry streaks, and whatever you draw on any strip changes the sound the next time the loop comes round. Behind the light the reader prints what the machine plays, a variable-area track along the bottom film, slowed so every cycle shows.
intent: Image is sound, after Daphne Oram's Oramics machine (https://www.daphneoram.org/?p=4469), where shapes drawn on strips of clear 35mm film set pitch and volume as they passed photocells, and Norman McLaren's Synchromy: what you see is what you hear.
